notes: Example configuration generated by the CraneCalc configurator; fictitious crane, supplier, survey and owner data, to be replaced with project data. Scope: 5 simply supported 25-ft bays, W27X84 + C15X33.9 girders, one 12.5-ton cab crane, bearing on the steps of the existing stepped columns (lower W30X173, upper W14X120) over the lower shafts' crane-side flanges, with top-flange ties to the upper shafts, the rail, bearings and end stops; the stepped columns are checked as two-shaft columns with their existing load effects (effective lengths from a buckling analysis), with the step's local checks, and the existing sidewall rod bracing takes the crane longitudinal forces. The paired flat bars on a direct flange saddle do not suit this capped girder (tie sizing ratio flange-tie-flange 4.78 > 1.00 for the estimated tie demands): the tie is the cap tieback angle bolted to the channel cap. Bumper overhang assumed 20 in (end-wheel centerline to the extended bumper face, a typical supplier proportion): the stop contact positions use it; confirm with the crane supplier. The existing cap-to-web fillets under the upper shaft's inner flange fail Category F throat fatigue (step-weld-fatigue 1.19, no bearing credit for an unfinished cap): a stiffener pair under the inner flange (J10.8), fitted to bear on the cap, the thinnest plate passing the stiffener checks; it carries the inner-flange force to the web on its own fillets (step-weld-fatigue 0.46 with it).

Lightest W and channel cap pair within the sizing targets (ratio ≤ 0.85, deflections ≤ 0.9 of the limits): screening estimates, H1 top-flange interaction with the load-height LTB strength ratio 0.82, vertical deflection 0.32, lateral 0.27 and rail-head movement with twist 0.50 of their limits; flanges at least 8.5 in wide for the end bearing bolt gauge and the rail seat; lighter candidates rejected: 130 by cap channel fit, 13 by sizing ratio, 230 by flange width; the next lighter, W18X97 + C12X20.7: W flange too wide for the channel with the weld pocket and tie room. These are the configurator's screening estimates (a simplified model that ranks the catalog), not the final ratios: the calculation checks the section and reports its own ratios.

fabrication.steel: W girder ASTM A992; cap channel and connection plates ASTM A572 Grade 50 unless noted.
fabrication.bolting: ASTM F3125 Grade A325, pretensioned, Class B faying surfaces, standard holes unless slots are detailed. Sliding-end bearing bolts and column-end tie bolts pretensioned against steel sleeves. Rail joints tight (gap 1/16 in max.), supplier's joint bars (deferred submittal) installed slip-critical: Class A surfaces, bolts pretensioned, re-tightened at 30 and 90 days.
fabrication.welding: E70XX low-hydrogen electrodes per AWS D1.1/D1.1M:2020, cyclically loaded provisions. Continuous fillets as dimensioned; no intermittent welds on cyclic load paths. Smooth starts and stops. Cap: continuous fillet each W top-flange edge, with the end development shown. Full cap bearing contact required. Bearing stiffeners CJP to the W top flange, bottom fitted.
fabrication.inspection: Visual inspection of all welds; AWS D1.1/D1.1M:2020 cyclically loaded acceptance criteria; magnetic particle testing of fillets at fatigue-sensitive attachments; 100% ultrasonic testing of CJP welds; bolt pretension verification per RCSC. Capped girder shop sequence: weld and UT the bearing stiffener CJPs and any under-flange attachments, check the top flange flatness, then fit and weld the cap.
fabrication.erection: Set and level the bearings, install the end bearings and flange ties, then set the rails. Provide temporary restraint until the permanent ties are complete.
fabrication.railAlignment: Set the rails to the specified gauge, alignment and level tolerances and survey them after erection, before the load test.
